issue: RETRACTED: two entries logged earlier today ('Indiana House 1992...47-55% below...', 'California district 50 and Texas district 16, 1992...') were FALSE POSITIVES caused by a bug in the NEW 1990/1992 FEC OCR parser (01dq_fec_1990_1992_house_parse.py), not real defects in our data. The OCR misread the state header 'IOWA' as '!OVA'; the parser's state-tracker did not reset, so Iowa's candidates and district total were attributed to the preceding state, Indiana -- and the reconciliation script SUMMED the resulting duplicate (state, district) totals (e.g. Indiana district 1: real total 211,824 + misattributed Iowa district 1 total 261,309 = the bogus 473,133 that looked like a 55% shortfall). Confirmed by hand against the Indiana Secretary of State's own 1992 general-election report (page images, R/data/indiana_sos_reports/indiana_election_report_1992.pdf): our data (147,054 + 64,770 = 211,824 for district 1) matches the state report exactly. The same duplicate-total pattern affected 60 of ~430 parsed 1992 districts (see the parser's own dedupe-by-dropping-duplicates fix, applied same day) and 8 of 1990's
evidence: Direct comparison of two independent sources on the SAME claim (our panel vs. the FEC book) that turned out to be a bug in the comparison tool, caught by re-reading the original Indiana state report page image
action: Fixed at the root: qa_state_reconcile_house_1990s.R now DROPS (rather than sums) any (state, district) key with more than one 'Total Votes:' hit in a single parse, since duplicates signal a missed state-header transition, not two genuine totals

issue: Corrected characterization: South Carolina House 1990 was NOT a data defect. The FEC's own scanned 1990 book gives district 5 (Spratt, unopposed) as 91,898 votes; South Carolina's own official 1990-91 election report (10 counties: Cherokee, Chester, Chesterfield, Fairfield, Kershaw, Lancaster, Laurens, Lee, Newberry, York) gives 78,362 and its own printed 'DISTRICT TOTALS' line matches the county rows exactly -- confirmed by reading the state report's page images directly (R/data/county_house_files/SC_Election_Report_1990-1991.pdf, pp.93-94). District 3 (Derrick D, Haskett R) shows the same pattern: the FEC book gives Derrick 72,561 and a district total of 125,050, while South Carolina's own canvass gives Derrick 86,103, Haskett 52,433 and a district total of 138,624 -- our release (138,616, 12 counties) matches the state canvass, not the FEC book. Our release uses the state's own canvass, which is internally consistent in both districts; the FEC's national compilation appears to be the one in error here, a rare case where the two official sources disagree and the state's own canvass looks more reliable
evidence: FEC book vs the SC Secretary of State's own printed district total (both read directly, not just totals)
action: Not a fix; noting for the record that the FEC's own historical books can themselves be wrong, which is why this project treats a single mismatch as a prompt to check further rather than as proof our data is wrong

issue: Confirmed as a genuine anomaly in the third-party source, not our processing: Oregon House 2002, Multnomah County's precinct file (openelections-data-or) gives Earl Blumenauer 267,620 votes in Multnomah ALONE, more than the FEC's certified total for his ENTIRE district (156,851, Multnomah + Clackamas combined). Checked directly against the raw file: each precinct's own row is internally consistent (candidate votes + write-in/over/under sum to that precinct's own printed 'Total' pseudo-row, which our pipeline correctly excludes), so this is not a rollup-duplication bug of the kind fixed elsewhere this session -- the raw per-precinct numbers themselves are implausibly high county-wide, for a reason not identified (possibly two elections' data concatenated, or a transcription error at the source). Districts 1, 2, 4 and 5 (which also include Multnomah or other affected counties) are off by 25-41%; district 3 by very nearly exactly 2x
evidence: FEC 'Federal Elections 2002' certified district totals (a clean, internally-consistent workbook) vs our county sums; raw OpenElections precinct file inspected directly

issue: FIXED (root cause of the Oregon House 2000s doubling previously only flagged): the precinct-level OpenElections source files for Oregon 2000/2002/2004 carry, in some counties, an EXTRA row per (office,district,party,candidate) with precinct=="Total" -- a county-wide rollup disguised as an ordinary precinct row, using the real candidate name, not caught by the existing pseudo-row filter (which only looks at the candidate field). Confirmed: Multnomah 2002 CD-3, Blumenauer's precinct=="Total" row (133,810 votes) exactly equals the sum of his ~110 real precinct rows. CD-3 sits entirely in Multnomah, which is why it had come out at ~2x; other 2000s districts span counties with and without the bug, so they were inflated 25-41% instead (as found by qa_state_reconcile_house_1990s.R). Not every county's file has this row (12/20 counties in 2000, 8/12 in 2002, 9/10 in 2004). Building the matching candidate-level long table and running check_long_vs_source also caught two smaller, unrelated pre-existing pseudo-candidate leaks on this state's own OpenElections wording: "Overvotes"/"Undervotes" written with no space (e.g. Gilliam 2004, 48 votes) and a bare "Blanks" candidate row (e.g. Clackamas 2002) -- both added to is_pseudo_row.
